correctness.rationale: From e(t)=D t²-Jt(s_left+s_right), strict stability is equivalent to D>J|h| at zero spins and sigma*h>D/J at nonzeros. All four D/J regimes and threshold equalities follow by exhaustive neighbor-sum cases. The alternating-block bijection gives the exact integer coefficients. The cyclic pointing series 2x f f_x/(1-f²) gives the unique dominant simple pole at x=1/lambda and, upon zero weighting, the vacancy-density limit. 72 independent exhaustive finite-volume comparisons and 26 formal renewal-coefficient comparisons passed. Experiments are explicitly not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: An explicit implication comparison distinguishes the present labeled one-dimensional strict absorbing-state polynomial from the two-dimensional low-temperature droplet minima of Cirillo–Olivieri (1995), the equilibrium one-dimensional partition functions of Almeida–Dalmazi (2005), mean-field periodically driven dynamics of Keskin–Canko–Kantar (2006), and two-state spin freezing. Existing binary-spin ring and three-spin-cycle classifications do not contain zero spins or the spin-one substitution conditions. Published-result alias and parameter searches supplied no matching claim; this is best-knowledge originality rather than a claim of database completeness.

value.rationale: Strict zero-temperature kinetic freezing of a three-state ferromagnet depends discontinuously on whether the crystal field permits stable vacancy-separated oppositely polarized domains. The complete exact finite-volume census, both neutral-move thresholds, exponential growth rate and typical vacancy density resolve a natural kinetic invariant beyond equilibrium transfer-matrix data and provide testable benchmarks for blocked states.
